extracted.intended_audience: open-source investigators, OSINT researchers, and prospective volunteer contributors to Bellingcat's toolkit
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and expectations for contributing, maintaining, and using entries in Bellingcat’s Online Open Source Investigation Toolkit — including who may contribute, what entries should contain, and maintenance/review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool entry content / availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Click on the name of a tool to view an in-depth review and guide for the tool (if available). You can also download this toolkit (or some of its categories) as a csv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool pages should include an in-depth review/guide when available; entries are organized by category and can be exported as CSV for offline use. The toolkit covers categories such as Maps & Satellites, Geolocation, Image/Video, Social Media, People, Websites, Companies & Finance, Conflict, Transport, Environment & Wildlife, Archiving, and Data Org & Analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff review before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Bellingcat staff checks each toolkit entry before it goes online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All volunteer-contributed entries are subject to staff review as a quality-control step prior to being published on the toolkit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer contributor expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are an expert for a specific category of open source research tools and you would like to contribute to this toolkit, get in touch with Johanna via toolkit@bellingcat.com. Feel free to introduce yourself and share a few words about your tool expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should demonstrate domain expertise for a specific toolkit category when applying; initial contact should include an introduction and brief summary of tool expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term volunteer commitment and update cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep in mind that contributing to our toolkit is a long-term volunteer commitment: You write tool descriptions and update them on a monthly basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors are expected to commit to ongoing maintenance of entries, with monthly updates to ensure accuracy and currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity verification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept volunteer contributors whose identity we don’t know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bellingcat requires that volunteer contributors be identifiable to the project team (some form of identity verification or known identity). Anonymous volunteers are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page maintainer disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If our Toolkit Maintainers choose to be publicly mentioned, you can find their names on individual tool pages under 'page maintainer'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintainers may opt into public attribution on individual tool pages; presence/absence of a public name is at the maintainer's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toolkit Guardian responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Toolkit Guardians have a special role: They help us further develop this toolkit to make sure it meets the needs of open source researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians are named volunteers/staff who oversee and develop category-level direction and ensure the toolkit aligns with community needs; examples and short bios of guardians are provided for several categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on tool suggestions via toolkit email
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not suggest tools that should be added to the toolkit via this e-mail address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The toolkit contact address (toolkit@bellingcat.com) is for contributor contact, feedback and questions, not for proposing new tools to be added; the page repeats this prohibition, implying there is an alternate process for tool suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility / cost note for users
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the tools that we include can be used for free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting or describing tools, the toolkit emphasizes availability and accessibility (many entries are for free tools); this may influence user expectations and selection of tools to include.
